read.sections.0.heading.source: A map shows a place from above

read.sections.0.text.note: "charts" (sea charts) is แผนที่เดินเรือ; Marshall Islands is หมู่เกาะมาร์แชลล์. "bus map" is แผนที่รถเมล์.
read.sections.0.text.source: A map is a drawing of a place, usually as a bird would see it from the sky. A map cannot show everything, so the mapmaker chooses what to include. For example, a bus map shows bus stops, and a rain map shows where it rains most. People have made maps for thousands of years. About 2,500 years ago, someone in today's Iraq made a map of the world on a clay tablet. It shows the city of Babylon in the middle. In the Marshall Islands in the Pacific Ocean, sailors made charts from sticks and shells. The sticks showed how ocean waves moved, and the shells showed islands.
read.sections.0.text.back: A map is a drawing of a place, usually drawn the way a bird would see it from the sky. A map can't show everything, so mapmakers choose what to put in. For example, a bus map shows bus stops, and a rain map shows where it rains the most. People have made maps for thousands of years. About 2,500 years ago, someone in the land that is Iraq today made a map of the world on a clay tablet. This map shows the city of Babylon in the centre. In the Marshall Islands in the Pacific Ocean, sailors made sailing maps from sticks and shells. The sticks show how ocean waves move, and the shells show where the islands are.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: A map is a picture of a place. It shows the place from above, like a bird sees it. A map cannot show everything. The person who makes it picks what to show. A bus map shows bus stops. People made maps long ago too. Someone in what is now Iraq made a map on clay. Sailors in the Marshall Islands made maps with sticks and shells. The shells showed islands.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: A map is a picture of a place. A map shows a place from above, like a bird sees it. A map can't show everything. Mapmakers choose what to show. A bus map shows bus stops. People have made maps for a long time. Someone in the land that is now Iraq made a map on clay. Sailors in the Marshall Islands made maps with sticks and shells. The shells show where the islands are.

read.sections.1.heading.source: Four tools help you read a map
read.sections.1.heading.back: Four tools help you read a map

read.sections.1.text.note: Thai has one school term for the map key, คำอธิบายสัญลักษณ์ (KEY_TERMS), so "which is also called a legend" is หรือที่บางคนเรียกว่าคำอธิบายแผนที่. "compass rose" is สัญลักษณ์ทิศ (KEY_TERMS, check).
read.sections.1.text.source: Most maps include four tools that help you read them. The title tells you what the map is about. The key, which is also called a legend, explains each symbol. A symbol is a colour, line or shape that represents something real. On the Riverstone map, a blue line is the river, and a green square is the community centre. The compass rose shows directions, and sometimes it is simply an arrow pointing north. The scale shows how distance on the map compares with real distance. On this map, one square is 100 metres, so the four-square footpath is about 400 metres long.
read.sections.1.text.back: Most maps have four tools that help you read them. The map title tells what the map is about. The key, which some people call the legend, explains what each symbol means. A symbol is a colour, line or shape that stands for something real. On the Riverstone map, the blue line is the river and the green square is the community centre. The compass rose shows directions. Sometimes it is just an arrow pointing north. The scale shows how distance on the map compares with real distance. On this map 1 square equals 100 metres, so a footpath four squares long is about 400 metres long.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: Most maps have four tools. The title says what the map is about. The key tells what each symbol means. A symbol is a small shape, line or colour. It stands for a real thing. On the Riverstone map, a blue line is the river. The compass rose shows north, south, east and west. The scale helps you see how far things are. Here, one square is 100 metres. The path to the centre is four squares. So it is about 400 metres long.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: Most maps have four tools. The map title tells what the map is about. The key tells what each symbol means. A symbol is a small shape, line or colour. It stands for a real thing. On the Riverstone map, the blue line is the river. The compass rose shows north, south, east and west. The scale helps you know how far things are. Here 1 square equals 100 metres. The path to the centre is four squares long, so it is about 400 metres long.

read.sections.2.text.source: The footpath from East Homes is about 400 metres, but the main-road route is about 700 metres, so the footpath is the shorter route. But is it the best route for every visitor? The map does not tell you if the path is muddy, if it has steps, or if it has lights at night. It also does not show whether the footbridge is open today. People who use the path every day know this information. A careful map reader uses the map as evidence and then asks local people who know the place. A map is extremely useful, but it is not the place itself.
read.sections.2.text.back: The footpath from East Homes is about 400 metres long, but the main road route is about 700 metres long. So the footpath is the shorter route. But is it the best route for every visitor? The map doesn't say whether the path is muddy, has steps, or has lights at night. The map also doesn't show whether the footbridge is open today. People who use this path every day know these things. A careful map reader uses the map as evidence, then asks local people who know the place. Maps are very useful, but a map is not the real place.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: The path over the bridge is 400 metres. The way by the road is 700 metres. So the path is the shorter route. But is it the best route? The map does not tell us everything. Is the path muddy? Does it have steps? Is it dark at night? People who walk there every day know. So look at the map first. Then ask people who know the place.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: The path over the bridge is 400 metres long. The way along the road is 700 metres long. So the path is the shorter route. But is it the best route? The map doesn't tell us everything. Is the path muddy? Are there steps? Is it dark at night? People who walk there every day know. So look at the map first, then ask people who know the place.

watch.summary.note: The explorer Steve Backshall is written สตีฟ แบ็กชอลล์ (a real person, read aloud; the checker warns that the Latin name does not appear: on purpose). "Ordnance Survey" kept in Latin with a short explanation (หน่วยงานที่ทำแผนที่ของเกรตบริเตน). Great Britain is เกรตบริเตน.
watch.summary.source: In this short video, the explorer Steve Backshall talks about map symbols. Ordnance Survey makes maps of Great Britain. Every Ordnance Survey map has a key, which is also called a legend. The key lists the symbols and says what each one means. A symbol is a small picture, line or colour. It stands for a real thing, like a path, a river or a building. Symbols save space, so a map can show a lot in a small area. When you know the symbols, you can understand a place before you go there. Maps from other mapmakers may use different symbols. So always read the key first.
watch.summary.back: In this short video, an explorer named Steve Backshall talks about map symbols. Ordnance Survey is the agency that makes maps of Great Britain. Every Ordnance Survey map has a key, also called a legend. The key lists the symbols and says what each one means. A symbol is a small picture, line or colour that stands for a real thing, such as a path, a river or a building. Symbols save space, so a map can show a lot of information in a small space. When you know the symbols, you can understand a place before you get there. Maps from other mapmakers may use different symbols, so always read the key first.
